name: Autoimmune/Inflammatory Optic Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Autoimmune Optic Neuropathy

criteria.description: Evidence of optic nerve inflammation demonstrated by clinical signs or imaging
Presence of systemic or organ-specific autoimmune markers or antibodies
Exclusion of infectious, ischemic, or compressive causes of optic neuropathy
Clinical improvement following immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory therapy
Characteristic visual field defects consistent with optic nerve involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of optic nerve inflammation plus autoimmune markers with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging and laboratory findings; response to immunotherapy supports diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral or bilateral optic disc swelling
searchTerms: optic disc swelling in one or both eyes
slow loss of sight without pain
pupil defect indicating optic nerve damage

common.symptomName: Visual field defects (central or altitudinal scotomas)
searchTerms: loss of central or upper/lower visual fields

common.symptomName: Periorbital discomfort or retro-orbital pain exacerbated by eye movement
searchTerms: eye socket pain worsened by eye movement

occasional.symptomName: Mild systemic constitutional symptoms (e.g., low-grade fever, malaise)
Mild optic nerve pallor in later stages
searchTerms: pale optic nerve in later disease
optic nerve color fading over time
optic nerve damage in both eyes at once
simultaneous vision nerve problems both sides

rare.symptomName: Associated autoimmune systemic manifestations (e.g., arthritis, rash)

laboratory: Presence of autoantibodies (ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB depending on associated autoimmune disease)
CSF analysis may show mild pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands
imaging: MRI of the orbits showing optic nerve enhancement and swelling
Exclusion of compressive lesions or ischemic changes
other: Visual evoked potentials showing delayed latency
Improvement with corticosteroids or immunosuppressive therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of optic nerve enhancement on MRI
Response to antimicrobial therapy rather than immunosuppression

redFlags: Severe optic nerve pallor with no improvement
Signs of systemic infection or malignancy
references: Optic Neuritis Treatment Trial Research Group. The clinical profile of optic neuritis. Arch Ophthalmol. 1991.
Jarius S, Wildemann B. Autoimmune optic neuropathies. Autoimmun Rev. 2015.
